resources.string: Hello %1$s, this is the About screen.
Tap an item to remove it.
No items yet. Add an item to get started.
Start either collector to receive 1, 2, and 3, half a second apart. Each collector starts its own sequence.
Try each screen, seed, and the hot flow. Each preview keeps its own state while you compare them.
Approach A: list stored directly in ViewModel
Approach B: list stored in ProfileData

Click quickly: each received event takes 500 ms. Switching patterns clears the displayed list and click count. ViewModel counters remain while retained; replay can deliver the last event again. Without a collector, only replayed events are retained.

Try this:
1. Press Increment several times.
2. Add items, then tap an item to remove it.

Expected behavior:
The counter changes only when you press Increment. Adding or removing list items does not change this independent counter. Rotate the device to check that the ViewModel keeps its state.

Try this:
1. Add several items.
2. Tap an item to remove it.
3. Rotate the device.

Expected behavior:
Each addition increases the counter by one. Removing an existing item decreases it by one. The list and counter remain together in the ViewModel.

Keyed list demo %1$d

Try this:
Add and remove items here, then change the other list demo on Home.

Expected behavior:
Each list has its own counter and items because it uses a different ViewModel key. Changing this demo must not change the other demo. Each addition increases its counter; each removal decreases it.

Starting seed: %1$d

Try this:
1. Add items and watch the counter.
2. Remove an item by tapping it.
3. Compare Seed 10 with Seed 20 in Screen previews.

Expected behavior:
The counter starts at the seed, increases for additions, and decreases for removals. The two seed destinations keep independent state.

Try this:
1. Start Collector 1.
2. Start Collector 2 before the first finishes.
3. After completion, start either collector again.

Expected behavior:
Each collector receives 1, 2, and 3 with a half-second delay between values. They run independent sequences. Restarting one does not change the other. Leaving the screen cancels active collection; rotation preserves the displayed latest values.

Try this:
1. Watch the counter for several seconds.
2. Navigate away, then return to the retained screen.

Expected behavior:
The ViewModel increases its StateFlow counter once per second without a button press. The counter continues while that ViewModel remains alive. A newly created ViewModel starts at zero; this is not permanent storage.

Exercise 6: simple StateFlow values

Try this:
Press Append To Name and Increment Counter, separately and repeatedly.

Expected behavior:
Each name click appends one x. Each counter click increases the number by one. The name and counter update independently and the UI immediately displays the latest values.

Exercise 7: an object in StateFlow

Try this:
Append to the name, increment the counter, then alternate the two buttons.

Expected behavior:
One state object holds both values. Changing the name preserves the counter; incrementing preserves the name. Each atomic update publishes a new snapshot that the UI displays.

Exercise 8: two list approaches

Try this:
1. Add several items in Approach A.
2. Add different items in Approach B.

Expected behavior:
Approach A stores a list directly in StateFlow. Approach B stores a list inside the profile state object. Both lists update immediately, but changing one does not change the other. Labels use a shortened timestamp, so duplicate labels are possible.

Exercise 9: SharedFlow

Try this:
1. Select Default and press Emit event rapidly.
2. Wait for the received list to catch up.
3. Repeat with Buffer 1: suspend and both drop-oldest patterns.
4. Leave Replay 1 and return to it.

Expected behavior:
Processing each received event takes 500 ms. With an active collector, the suspend patterns eventually receive every emitted event in order. Drop-oldest patterns can skip queued labels. Replay 1 delivers the last retained event to a returning collector. Switching patterns clears the displayed clicks and list, but retained ViewModels keep their numbering. Without a collector, only replay values are retained.

Day 25, slides 17–21

Try this:
1. Launch Android and check Logcat: Hello appears before World!, one second later. This console experiment intentionally delays startup.
2. Press Click me and check Logcat for the same delayed output, this time without blocking the UI.
3. Press Change user. Press it again before the one-second fetch completes.
4. Leave the screen while work is pending.

Expected behavior:
The button launches work in a remembered composition scope. The profile displays Loading... and then the current User label. Changing the user cancels the previous LaunchedEffect fetch and starts another. Leaving composition cancels pending UI work. The fetch is a delay-based mock, not a network request.

Try this:
1. Choose an exercise chip. Swipe the chip row sideways to see all exercises.
2. Use the Info icon inside that exercise for its steps.
3. Press Open full screen to navigate to its normal destination.

Expected behavior:
You interact with the real exercise inside the preview. ViewModel-backed previews have separate owners, so changing one does not change another. Local composition-only state can reset when switching. Back from a full-screen exercise returns to the preview destination.

Navigation and route arguments

Try this:
Read the supplied name, open Contact, then use Back.

Expected behavior:
About displays the name passed to its destination. Contact opens with its own supplied person data. Back returns to the previous entry; the shared navigation bars remain available.

Navigation with two arguments

Try this:
Read the supplied name and city. Navigate to About or Home, then use Back.

Expected behavior:
Contact displays both values supplied to its route. Back reveals the previous entry. These are sample values, not a real contact or network lookup.
